CASE BRIEFING

Murder at the Manor

A dinner party. Six famous innovators. One murder.

Here’s a reminder of your mission:

YOUR MISSION

    How to solve the case

    1. Each guest is being held in a different room of the manor. Open any room.
    2. Read the guest’s file. Answer its three questions. Each answer fills a row of letter boxes.
    3. Copy the numbered letters, in number order, to decode a witness clue.
    4. The witness describes a different guest. Choose who you think it is and whether they have an alibi. An alibi places a guest somewhere else at 8:00. If you have not read about that guest yet, leave it blank and come back later.
    5. After all six rooms, open the Case Board. Name the murderer and open the safe.

    You can go back into any room at any time. Your answers are saved on this computer. To carry on from a different computer or browser, press Save progress at the top of the page and write down your code.

    The household

    The staff are your witnesses.

    The party, the murder, the household, and the letter are invented, and these six were never together in one room. The guests and their work are real.

    Type your first name. It shows at the top of every screen and on your case-closed certificate.

    The manor

    No one leaves until the case is solved. Each guest is being held in a different room. Visit the rooms in any order: read the guest’s ideas, answer three questions, then decode a witness clue. Each witness describes a different guest.

      Record what this witness tells you

      This witness describes a different guest from the one whose room you just solved. Use the decoded clue and the guest files to work out who it is.

      Select the guest whose ideas fit the statement. If you have not read their file yet, leave this for later.

      The host was killed in the study at 8:00. Choose Yes if the witness places this guest somewhere else at that time. Choose No if the statement does not account for the guest at 8:00. Seeing someone earlier is not enough by itself. If you are unsure, leave it for later.
